 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Narsing Rao Nandikonda
 M.A.C.M.A.No.518 of 2020

sentences.text: Judgment:

This M.A.C.M.A. is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellant/claimant aggrieved by the Award and decree dated 23.01.2020 passed in M.V.O.P.No.273 of 2016 by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Nalgonda,
(for short, 'the Tribunal') seeking compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 14.03.2016.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Nalgonda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are that appellant/claimant filed M.V.O.P.No.273 of 2016 under Section 166(1)(a) of the M.V.Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries received in a motor vehicle accident alleged to have caused due to rash and negligent manner by the Scorpio car bearing No.MH 16 BM 1715.

It is contended that on 14.03.2016, the petitioner and some others were travelling in an Auto bearing No.AP 24 TC 1417 from Thirumalagiri Village to Imampet Village and when the auto reached the outskirts of Vallabhapuram Village, the NNR,J driver of Scorpio Car bearing No.MH 16 BM 1715 came in high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed the auto from back side, due to which the petitioner sustained fracture of left femur, fracture of left leg hip joint, fracture of left shoulder, head injury and grievous injuries on all over the body.

The petitioner was immediately taken to Government Area Hospital, Suryapet, from there he was shifted to Kamineni Hospital,
Narketpally, wherein he underwent treatment as in patient for about fifteen days i.e., from 15.03.2016 to 30.03.2016.
After the discharge from hospital, he is continuing treatment in private hospitals and incurred huge amounts towards medical expenses.

The petitioner was hale and healthy and was earning Rs.10,000/- a mason and due to the said accident, he was unable to do his day to day work as he became permanently disabled, he could not move from bed.

Basing on a complaint, crime No.44 of 2016 was registered for the offence punishable under Section 338 of Indian Penal Code against the driver of the offending vehicle and after due investigation, police have filed charge sheet vide C.C.No.520 of 2016 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class Suryapet.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class Suryapet
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: NNR,J 3.
Before the learned Tribunal, Respondent No.1 the driver of the crime vehicle and Respondent No.3 added as owner-cum-driver of auto were remained exparte.

The respondent No.2 - United India Insurance Company Limited filed their counter-affidavit, denying all the averments made in the claim petition, including the manner in which the accident took place, age, avocation and income of the petitioner and and further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

sentences.text:
4. Basing on the pleadings and averments made by both the counsels, the learned Tribunal framed the following issues which reads as under:
"i) Whether the claimant sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of the Scorpio bearing No.MH 16 BM 1715 by its driver?
2. Whether the claimant is entitled for compensation, and if so, to what amount and from whom?

3. To what relief?"
5.

After perusing the oral and documentary evidence and going into the entire record and the evidence placed by both the parties, the NNR,J learned Tribunal allowed the claim in part and granted compensation of Rs.2,43,360/- along with interest @ 9%
per annum.

6. Being unsatisfied and aggrieved by the meager compensation amount awarded by the learned Tribunal, the present appeal is filed on the following ground among other grounds that the learned Tribunal did not choose to consider that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries with fractures and that he has incurred more than Rs.4,00,000/- and was in hospital for more than fifteen days as inpatient.
The learned Tribunal ought to have granted Rs.4,00,000/- with interest and also the loss of earning, medical bills and transportation charges.

The learned Tribunal ought to have considered the disability assessed by PWs 2 & 3 and the disability certificate i.e.,
Ex.A8 issued by PW3 who is a Doctor/Member of the Medical Board assessing the disability at 40%.

The learned Tribunal ought to have taken the income of the petitioner at Rs.10,000/- as the petitioner was a mason and was earning Rs.10,000/-
but the learned Tribunal has taken only Rs.8,000/-.
a reasonable amount towards pain and sufferance.
The learned Tribunal has awarded meager amount of Rs.40,000/- towards pain and sufferance.
Though the petitioner has placed the relevant certificates NNR,J issued by the doctors that the petitioner has occurred huge amounts towards medical expenses.
07. Heard Sri C.Mohan Prakash, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Ch.Venkata Narayana, learned counsel for the respondent No.2.
Perused the material on record.
08. Admittedly, respondents have not filed cross-appeal against the Award passed by the learned Tribunal.
As such, there is no dispute regarding liability of the respondents and occurrence of the accident.

The only point that arose before this Court in this appeal is that:
i) Whether the petitioner is entitled for the enhanced compensation, if so, to what extent?

sentences.text: Admittedly, the present appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant having been unsatisfied with the compensation awarded by the learned Tribunal i.e., Rs.2,43,360/- as against the claim of the appellant/claimant i.e., Rs.4,00,000/-.

Admittedly, there is no dispute regarding the nature of accident and the involvement of the said Scorpio Car and there is also no dispute with the fact that the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2.
It is also not in dispute that the said NNR,J accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the said Scorpio Car.

The main grievance of the petitioner is that the learned Tribunal ought to have taken the income of the petitioner at Rs.10,000/- which the petitioner has claimed, but the learned Tribunal has taken the income of the petitioner @ Rs.8,000/- as the petitioner was a mason and was earning Rs.10,000/-.
10.
It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has placed relevant material to show that the petitioner was a mason by examining himself as PW-1.
Though the learned Tribunal having considered that the petitioner was a mason but the learned Tribunal did not chose to consider the income of the petitioner @ Rs.10,000/-, but taken as Rs.8,000/-.

It is also held that there is no evidence placed in respect of wage slips and the learned Tribunal considering the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act and also the Rules governing therein and has taken the income of the petitioner @ Rs.8,000/- per month and assessed the compensation.

11. The other ground raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the learned Tribunal did not considered the 25% of the future NNR,J prospects which has to be added to the income of the petitioner.

This Court having taken the income of the petitioner as Rs.8,000/- and adding 25% of the income towards future prospects as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Corporation Vs. Pranay Sethi 1 which is relevant to the age group of 40-50 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Corporation Vs. Pranay Sethi 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The actual income of the petitioner would be Rs.10,000/- per month.

Taking the said income,
this Court would like to venture for reassessment of compensation.
It is also not in dispute that the petitioner sustained 40% disability, and the learned Tribunal has rightly taken the same as 40%.

It is also the grievance of the petitioner that the learned Tribunal ought not to have deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses which is not prescribed under the cases of injuries, in the opinion of this Court, the learned Tribunal has erred in taking 1/3rd of the income towards personal expenses is the error committed by the learned Tribunal and the income of the petitioner would be Rs.8,000/- +
Rs,2000/- (25%) = Rs.10,000/- x 12 = 1,20,000/-.
The relevant multiplier for the age group of 40-45 years, taking the age of the petitioner @ 43 years, as per the medical report, it shows that the (2017 AACJ 2700 (SC)).

NNR,J petitioner's age is 42 to 43 and as per the affidavit filed before this Court, the age of the petitioner is shown as 40 years, as such the age of the petitioner can be taken in between 41 to 45 years and the relevant multiplier applicable would be 14.
After taking the disability, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income = 10,08,000.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,08,000/- towards loss of future income.

sentences.text:
The only dispute raised by the appellant before this Court is only two aspects i.e.,
non-consideration of 25% of future prospects and deducting 1/3rd of income towards personal expenses and as the said aspects has been answered and further taking into the consideration of the assessment made by this Court, the petitioner in all would be entitled for compensation of Rs.10,86,000/- including the amounts which are awarded by the learned Tribunal i.e., loss of income during treatment Rs.8,000/-, loss of amenities Rs.30,000/- and pain and sufferance Rs.40,000/-.
NNR,J 13.

On overall re-appreciation of the pleadings, material on record and submissions made by both sides, this Court is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled to enhancement of compensation as modified and recalculated as above and as given in the table below for easy reference.
Amount arrived at Amount arrived at  Head by the Tribunal by this Court  Loss of future income Rs.1,65,360/- Rs.10,08,000/-

Loss of income during Rs.8,000/- Rs.8,000/-
 treatment  Loss of amenities Rs.30,000/- Rs.30,000/-
 Pain & sufferance Rs.40,000/- Rs.40,000/-
 Total Rs.2,43,360/- Rs.10,86,000/-
14.
By considering the observation of Hon'ble Apex Court in Nagappa Vs.Gurudayal Singh 2, the compensation can be awarded more than the claimed amount".
Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to the enhanced compensation of Rs.10,86,000/- as against the awarded amount of Rs.2,43,360/- by the learned Tribunal.
15. Considering the circumstances of the case, the learned Tribunal has rightly awarded the rate of interest at 9% per annum and the same needs no interference by this Court.

Hence, this Court is of the opinion 2003 (2) SCC 274 NNR,J that the petitioner/claimant is entitled to interest @ 9% per annum on the enhanced amount.
16.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.10,86,000/-.

Accordingly,
the M.A.C.M.A is allowed, enhancing the compensation from Rs. 2,43,360/- to Rs.10,86,300/- with interest at the rate @ 9 % p.a. on the enhanced amount from the date of petition till the date of realization.

The respondents are directed to deposit the said amount together with costs and interest after giving due credit to the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

However, the petitioner is directed to pay the Deficit Court Fee on the enhanced amount within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this Jittaboina Nagaiah vs Nalawade Ashok Dattatray on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9912625/
